description: VM-side operating facts for the Nabatable local CI runner, read by scripts/ci/executor/config.ts (loadOperatingFacts) and infra/local-ci/bin/*.sh. Scheduling policy (dedicated window, nightly start, disk caps, retention, polling, heartbeat, fallback) is owned by config/ci/operating-config.json and the controller; this file only names the physical shape the controller and executor drive and points back at the policy source.

policySource.rule: Values that appear in config/ci/operating-config.json are never copied here. Fields below that say `source` are JSON pointers into that file; the controller resolves them at runtime and the VM side must not read them independently.

window.vmSideBehaviour: Inside the dedicated window the controller runs job instances in mode `dedicated`, otherwise `normal`. Job instances never persist between requests, so there is nothing to pause or resume at the window edge: a request that overruns is aborted and its instance destroyed.

runtime.qualificationNote: Hosted workflows run Node 22; production Vercel runs Node 24. The job image stays on node22 until the Node 24 candidate image has passed the Phase 2 qualification list in docs/runbooks/local-ci.md and the package engines/workflow node-version are flipped in a reviewed release.

image.requestTupleDigestRule: The request tuple's imageDigest (NABATABLE_CI_IMAGE_DIGEST, stamped by the controller) is the job image digest, the sha256 in NABATABLE_CI_JOB_IMAGE; the executor rejects a request whose imageDigest differs from the image it runs. The golden disk digest (NABATABLE_CI_BASE_IMAGE_DIGEST) is a separate executor-only check.

network.phaseRule: Job containers can reach the proxy only while the executor holds the guest in phase `prep` (sudo -n egress.sh phase prep); phase `test` empties the gate chain in both directions and the executor verifies `egress.sh status` reports `phase: test` before running repository code.

controller.keychainRule: Every item is a generic password with service = item name and account = keychainAccount (`security add-generic-password -s <item> -a nabatable-ci -w`). githubAppPrivateKey holds the PEM verbatim or as single-line base64; controller.sh copies it into a 0600 file under ~/nabatable-ci/run and exports its path as privateKeyPathEnv for the controller. The executor reads the two R2 items by the names above.
